newsitem.title: UK: Kingfisher lower despite Xmas sales cheer.
newsitem.headline: Kingfisher lower despite Xmas sales cheer.

text.p: Retailing group Kingfisher Plc saw its shares stuck lower in a broadly positive market on Tuesday, despite general reports of Christmas spending reaching the boom levels last seen in the 1980s.
After a recent strong run on the back of a positive third quarter trading update, Kingfisher has slid lower and was down 8-1/2 pence at 627-1/2.
Analysts could not pinpoint any particular reason for the soft share price, which bucked the upbeat sector trend.
Other fellow retailers were ahead in line with market gains, with Argos up 10 1/2 pence at 786 and Marks and Spencer up seven pence at 492.
One analyst said despite the positive outlook for Christmas sales in the UK, not all of Kingfisher's divisions would benenfit.

The main beneficiaries in the group are the Woolworth general goods chain and the Comet electrical goods division. But, do-it-yourself retailer B&Q will enjoy little feed-through, said SocGen analyst Robert Snaith.

Its French electrical retailer Darty is seen suffering not just from strong sterling levels, but also from a sickly French economy, he said. economy," with reverberations felt in the French consumer market, he said.
Analysts dismissed some commentary that the share weakness could stem from a UK television documentary report on Monday, which criticised allegedly anti-competitive electrical retailing practices.

The issue was already under review by competition watchdog the Office of Fair Trading. But one market watcher said even if it was a damaging report, the effect on Comet was likely to be minimal in the context of total group profits. Also other rivals in the sector like Dixons Plc remained steady.
